questions.question: What problem does positional encoding solve in Transformer models?
choices: It reduces the number of parameters needed in the model
It gives the model awareness of token order, since self-attention alone is permutation-invariant
It replaces the need for tokenization
It speeds up the training process by skipping layers
questions.explanation: Self-attention treats input as a set, not a sequence — it doesn't know that 'I love cats' differs from 'cats love I'. Positional encoding injects position information so the model understands token order.

questions.question: What are the key properties of sinusoidal positional encoding?
choices: It uses random values that change each training step
It uses sine and cosine functions of different frequencies, allowing the model to learn relative positions via linear transformations
It assigns a fixed integer to each position and adds it directly to the embedding
It only works for sequences shorter than 512 tokens
questions.explanation: Sinusoidal encoding uses sine for even dimensions and cosine for odd dimensions at varying frequencies. This allows the model to attend to relative positions because PE(pos+k) can be expressed as a linear function of PE(pos).

questions.question: Why does sinusoidal positional encoding allow models to generalize to sequence lengths not seen during training?
choices: Because it uses learned embeddings that interpolate between positions
Because the sinusoidal pattern is periodic and predictable, so the model can extrapolate to longer positions
Because it pads all sequences to a fixed length
Because it only encodes relative positions, not absolute ones
questions.explanation: Sinusoidal functions produce a deterministic, periodic pattern. Since the pattern extends mathematically beyond training lengths, the model can generalize to longer sequences without retraining.
